1.Nf3 Nf6 2.c4 g6 3.g3 Bg7 4.Bg2 O-O 5.O.strategy: Brings another piece into the fight for the centre: the knight eyes d5 and supports a later central advance. White keeps the pressure on the d5 square while every pawn structure remains possible, so Black has to be precise about what to allow.
Develops the knight to its best square, covering d4 and e5, so White cannot build a pawn centre cheaply. A slow, symmetrical manoeuvring game follows: solid equality for Black, with little to attack.
